title: Write draft-atwood-jmap-chat-did companion draft
description:
Optional companion draft delivering actual DID interop, separable from the core JMAP Chat spec.

CONTEXT

q15f resolved 2026-05-12 with Option B: the core spec acknowledges DID URIs as a valid form of ChatContact.id (commit 48b6a31) but does not define DID resolution, auth, or any new capability. This bead is the deferred Option C work — a separate companion draft that defines those mechanics for deployments that want real DID interop. Filing it now keeps the option preserved without committing to a timeline; it can land whenever there's appetite without disrupting anything else.

The companion-draft approach is preferred over inlining DID support into the core spec because:
- Core spec stays minimal and reviewable
- Deployments that don't care about DIDs ignore the companion entirely
- DID-first deployments (AT Protocol-adjacent) adopt the companion incrementally
- The work is reversible: if the spec fails to land or a better DID standard supersedes it, the core spec is unaffected

SCOPE

The draft would define (filing the rough table of contents here; finalize when writing begins):

1. Capability URN: `urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:did`. Advertised in session capabilities and per-account accountCapabilities. Empty object at session level; account level may carry policy fields (supported DID methods, resolution cache TTL, etc.).

2. ChatContact extensions: optional `did` field on ChatContact, populated when the contact's id is itself a DID URI OR when a separate DID identity is bound to the contact. Spec the interaction with the core spec's opaque-id rule.

3. Federation auth model: how a peer server authenticates as a DID-controlled principal. Likely candidates:
   - mTLS + DID document binding (peer cert's identity resolves to the DID's keys)
   - OAuth 2.0 + DID claim in token (token presented to the local server includes a verified DID claim)
   - Direct cryptographic signature using the DID's verification method
   Decision needed: which mechanism is mandatory-to-implement.

4. DID method support: which DID methods are mandatory vs MAY. Recommend starting with `did:web` (DNS-based resolution, lowest implementation complexity). `did:key` (no resolution needed; self-contained) is a natural second. Heavier methods (`did:plc`, `did:ion`, `did:ethr`) MAY be supported but not mandatory.

5. Resolution rules: when a server encounters a DID, when does it resolve? Cache TTL? Stale-key handling? Revocation?

6. Companion ChatContact resolution flow: how clients/servers turn a DID into a ChatContact.id and serverUrl. Probably uses DID Document service entries.

7. Possible @{did} mention textual form: overlap with f13f (federated user mention @user@host). The two forms can coexist: @user@host is the DNS-resolvable form, @{did} is the DID-resolvable form. Mention type at the wire level is still `type: "user"` with the id field carrying either form.

8. IANA considerations: capability URN registration.

OPEN DESIGN DECISIONS (would become sub-beads when writing begins)

- Which DID auth mechanism is mandatory-to-implement?
- Which DID methods are mandatory? (recommend did:web)
- ChatContact.did as a separate field vs DID embedded in ChatContact.id?
- Resolution caching strategy?
- @{did} mention textual form: coordinate with f13f or independent?
- Companion guide (jmap-chat-did-implementer-guide.md) — file as separate bead or fold into this?

FORWARD COMPATIBILITY

This bead does not disturb q15f's Option B prose sentence. That sentence already permits DID URIs as ChatContact.id values; this companion draft adds the auth/resolution/policy layer on top. Deployments using only the core spec (with q15f's accommodation) and deployments adopting this companion are both conformant; the companion is additive.

If interest is low when work begins, the draft can be shipped narrower (e.g., did:web only, no resolution caching detail, no @{did} mention form) and expanded later. Future revisions can add more DID methods and more elaborate auth.

REFERENCES

- W3C DID-Core (already an informative reference in main draft after commit 48b6a31)
- did:web method spec (https://w3c-ccg.github.io/did-method-web/)
- did:key method spec (https://w3c-ccg.github.io/did-method-key/)
- AT Protocol identity model (informative; not a normative dependency)
acceptance_criteria:
- draft-atwood-jmap-chat-did-00.md exists as a standalone IETF-style Internet-Draft
- Capability URN `urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:did` defined and IANA-registration-ready
- At least one DID method (recommended: did:web) specified as mandatory-to-implement; others MAY
- DID-based federation auth model specified, with the mandatory mechanism unambiguously chosen
- ChatContact extensions (whether 'did' is a separate field or embedded in 'id') spec'd
- Cross-references with the main draft consistent with q15f's Option B prose acknowledgement (commit 48b6a31); no contradiction
- Companion implementer guide: either included in scope of this bead, or filed as a separate dependent bead with rationale
- Open design decisions listed above each have a documented chosen answer before final draft text
